messages.subject: DSM: 2D X,Y smooths
parts:
Hello listfolk!

I am currently using DSM to estimate abundance of cetaceans in the Maldives. I am running into some minor issues and was hoping someone here might be able to give me some advice.
I have attached my model, summary and smooth plots. Essentially, with an (X,Y) 2D smooth, the model is showing high abundance in an extrapolated region. Is there any protocol for selecting/ number of knots for 2d contours that anyone may know of?
Any and all help is greatly appreciated!

Many thanks,
Isha

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM: 2D X,Y smooths
parts:
Isha

If extrapolation is of concern to you, I suggest you investigate the dsmextra package

https://densitymodelling.github.io/dsmextra/
A Toolkit for Extrapolation Assessments in Density Surface Models
User-friendly tools for the detection and assessment of extrapolation in multivariate environmental space (Bouchet et al. 2019), with applications to density surface models of line transect data. Provides convenience functions for summarising and visualising extrapolation in prediction areas.
densitymodelling.github.io
Regarding the amount of smoothing in your 2D smooth, consult this wiki devoted to spatial modelling questions
https://osf.io/wgc4f/wiki/mgcv:%20model%20selection/
